trust_decision.summary: Descriptor web methods that return Contrast connection profiles, vulnerability types and application IDs must be callable only by a user allowed to configure the relevant scope; at the pinned commit the decision is made (or not made) per method inside each of five descriptors, never in the shared helper that actually produces the data.

landing_point.why: doFillTeamServerProfileNameItems has no permission check at all while its neighbours in three other descriptors already carry a (wrongly scoped) one; a reader of the advisory summary greps doFill* and lands here first.

fix_sites.entry_point: descriptorByName/ContrastAgentStep/fillProfileItems (contrastAgent pipeline step form, also Snippet Generator)

job property descriptor at global scope

O3_reason_to_dismiss: It is not a form-fill endpoint but a JavaScript proxy method bound into the recorder's own config page, and it only returns one boolean profile flag, so a solver can argue the page is already behind job Configure and the method is not a data sink.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A user holding only Item.CONFIGURE on a job must still get populated profile/application/rule dropdowns on that job's config page, and pipeline-step dropdowns rendered with no Item ancestor must still work for administrators; a fix that simply demands Jenkins.ADMINISTER everywhere (which is effectively what the pinned tree's existing guard does) hides both.

O6_input_shapes: item ancestor present and holding Item.CONFIGURE (job config page)
no item ancestor at all (global config page, Snippet Generator, proxy call outside a job) -> requires Jenkins.ADMINISTER
same descriptor reached at global scope versus job scope (descriptorByName at root versus on a job)
two calling conventions: form fill (doFill*/doCheck*) and @JavaScriptMethod proxy invocation
the profile-name parameter (teamServerProfileName / profile) is caller-controlled, so the guard has to be independent of it, and in the fix it is
teamServerUrl shape: an empty host is now rejected and the message says URL (secondary non-permission hunk in ContrastPluginConfig.doTestTeamServerConnection)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Descriptor getter getTeamServerProfiles() hands back the persisted Contrast profiles (name, username, orgUuid, teamServerUrl, apps) with no permission check; used by global.jelly and by VulnerabilityTrendHelper.getProfileNames()
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a plain getter for the config form rather than a fill/check endpoint, so a solver can say the security review covered doFill*/doCheck* methods and that Jenkins core already guards the page that uses it.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the global-config sites, one package hop from the recorder landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Descriptor getter getConditions() returns the last-saved ThresholdCondition list (application ids, vulnerability types, statuses) for the whole instance with no permission check
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is the recorder descriptor's own state accessor for the config form, not a validation route, and it carries no explicit permission contract.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an unchecked doFillApplicationNameItems(profile) beside doFillSeverityItems that returns profile-derived application names
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The step already accepts applicationName as a @DataBoundSetter (VulnerabilityTrendStep.java:75-80) and its form has a profile select, so a maintainer adding a name dropdown there would copy the neighbouring unchecked shape.

This descriptor already receives the profile by @RelativePath for two other fill methods, so an application-title dropdown is a one-line copy of doFillApplicationIdItems and easy to add without the guard.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second @JavaScriptMethod (for example getApplicationIds(profile)) on the same bound descriptor
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: config.jelly already binds the descriptor into JavaScript (config.jelly:174-179) and calls the existing proxy method on profile change, so extending that script with another proxy call is natural and has no form-level permission hook to copy.

O9_family: CWE-862 missing authorization (Jenkins descriptor web-method permission checks)

O10_build.toolchain: Maven, jenkins parent 5.31, jenkins.version 2.479.3, plugin BOM bom-2.479.x, JDK 21 in CI
O10_build.project_tests: JUnit4 with Mockito/PowerMock under src/test/java (8 classes at the pinned commit: VulnerabilityTrendHelperTest, VulnerabilityTrendStepTest, ContrastPluginConfigTest, ContrastPluginConfigSecurityTest, ThresholdConditionTest, VulnerabilityTrendRecorderTest, plus stubs); no JenkinsRule integration tests; CI runs 'mvn -B -Dfindbugs.skip=true clean test' (build.yml:23)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Copy the existing 'Jenkins.getActiveInstance().hasPermission(Item.CONFIGURE)' guard from the neighbouring doFill* methods onto the five unprotected ones, leaving the check global-instance-scoped and adding no item ancestor.

out_of_scope_notes: TeamServerProfile keeps apiKey/serviceKey in Secret fields (TeamServerProfile.java:19-21) and exposes them through getSecretApiKey/getSecretServiceKey; whether any descriptor getter serializes them is a credential-exposure question (CWE-522/200), outside this advisory's permission-check scope, and was not pursued.

ThresholdCondition.doCheckApplicationId and doFillApplicationIdItems make the server call the TeamServer with stored credentials (ThresholdCondition.java:280-293, 306-315); server-side request behaviour was not pursued.
unverified: ACL semantics of Jenkins.hasPermission(Item.CONFIGURE) were not exercised at runtime; the claim that it is instance-scoped and denies non-administrators is inferred from the fix replacing it with item.hasPermission(Item.CONFIGURE) plus a Jenkins.ADMINISTER fallback.

Repo size in MB was not measured (no shell tool); the pinned tree is 19 Java files, 10 Jelly files and about 70 tracked paths in total, so the tiny_repo reading rests on that inventory rather than on a byte count.
The build was not executed (no shell, no Docker): resolution of the Jenkins parent POM, plugin BOM and test dependencies from repo.jenkins-ci.org is unverified.
Stapler property-level routing of getTeamServerProfiles() and getConditions() on a Descriptor was not exercised; whether an unauthenticated HTTP caller can read those values as JSON is unverified.
Whether @RequirePOST on ThresholdCondition.doFillApplicationIdItems matches how the Jenkins combobox AJAX issues its request was not exercised.
